claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 11 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with you.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your residency status:

**Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another immigration status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure what you mean by that - I live here in the UK with my son. Is there something specific you need to know about my situation?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I apologize for any confusion. Let me ask this more simply:

**Were you born in the UK, or did you move here from another country?**

This helps me understand if there are any additional residency requirements I need to check for your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm sorry, but I don't actually have that information in my situation. I can tell you that I live in the UK with my son Alex, but I haven't been told whether I was born here or moved here from another country.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly fine. Let me ask about a few other aspects of your situation to assess eligibility:

**Is Alex in full-time education or does he attend school?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's 11, so he's in school - he goes to primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a few more questions:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex? In other words, do you provide for his day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and housing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. He lives with me and I look after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to check a couple more things:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex (for example, Alex's other parent or another family member)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I don't know if anyone else is claiming for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask a few final questions:

**Has Alex ever been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, or been in hospital or residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't been in care or hospital like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Does Alex work for 24 hours or more per week, or does he receive any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work - he's only 11! And he doesn't get any benefits himself.

## Eligibility Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✓ **Alex is 11 years old** - under the age limit of 16 (or 20 if in approved education)
✓ **You live in the UK** with Alex
✓ **Alex lives with you** and you're responsible for his day-to-day care
✓ **Alex attends school** (approved education)
✓ **No disqualifying factors** - Alex isn't in long-term care or hospital, doesn't work 24+ hours per week, and doesn't receive benefits in his own right

### Important points to note:

1. **Only one person can claim** - If someone else (like Alex's other parent) is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, they would need to stop their claim before you could claim. You should check this before applying.

2. **High Income Tax Charge** - If you or your partner earn over £60,000 individually, you may have to pay a tax charge on the Child Benefit received.

3. **How to apply** - You can apply for Child Benefit through the government website or by contacting HMRC.

Would you like any more information about applying or have any other questions?
